To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) machine learning can be useful for text generation; (2) the features that predict cue usage in tutorial explanations are different from those that predict cue usage for general expository text; (3) the features that are most important in predicting cue usage are different for different cues; and (4) the decision trees we induced can be used to generate text that is more like the original corpus than the text generated by the current version of a rule-based system.
machine learning can identify features predictive of discourse cues, and that these features can be used to improve the generation of explanations.

the features with the most predictive power for cue occurrence and cue placement are: the type of cue, the number of cues in the sentence, the sentence length, the type of sentence, and whether the cue is a conjunction or a discourse connective.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
What features of a discourse situation affect the choice of a particular cue?
developing a theory of cue usage in tutorial explanations.
identifying features that predict the use of discourse cues and with applying a machine learning program to induce rules from a corpus of coded data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the machine learning approach to text generation is a viable one, and that C4.5 can be used effectively to induce decision trees that can be used for text generation.

the use of machine learning to induce decision trees from a corpus of tutorial explanations is useful in identifying features that predict cue usage, and in identifying the features with most explanatory power for cue occurrence and cue placement.
the results of our experiments are promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of the experiments show that machine learning programs are useful for text generation and that the features identified as being most useful are those that have been previously thought to affect discourse cue usage.
machine learning can help in the design of a system that generates explanations for tutorial dialogues.
we have developed a new methodology for text generation that combines the strengths of machine learning and knowledge representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the features we used to predict cue usage are the same ones that we have used to generate explanations in the past, but the relative importance of these features is different than what we expected.
the features that best predict cue occurrence and placement in tutorial explanations are not the same ones previously thought to be important.
the features that predict discourse cue usage are not the same as the features that predict cue placement.
